summary: Multnomah County summit lookout: a 1914-15 timber platform, a 1920s steel tower, a 1940s L-4 cab; removed in 1976. The summit is now a public day-use area.

facts.design: Aermotor steel tower with 7x7 steel cab (1924), later a timber tower with an L-4 cab
facts.status_note: The lookout was removed in 1976; the summit is now a public day-use area.

access.note: The summit picnic area and Sherrard Point viewpoint are open; Larch Mountain Road closes seasonally from November to May or June.

visit.trail_note: Sherrard Point Trail #443 is a paved 0.2-mile trail from the picnic area, with about 100 steps to the viewpoint.

events.note: Register date: platform and cab on top of two 90 ft fir trees
Newspapers show the tower finished by June and recently erected by October 1915; firelookout.com also gives 1915
Register date: 90 ft steel tower with metal cab and ground house; materials stored in November 1923 for spring erection
firelookout.com date for the steel tower; Forest Lookouts chronology: 90 ft Aermotor tower with 7x7 steel cab
Wilbur Harrison (spelled Wilbert in the 1934 and 1937 items) lookout in 1934 and 1935; still there in 1937
Aircraft Warning Service station Tare 2-9 active from October 1942 to October 1943; the Forest Service kept the site for fire detection
Mid-1940s timber tower with L-4 cab and public observation deck; sources give 84, 90 or 100 ft

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 1914 for the first platform and cab, firelookout.com gives 1915, and the 1915 newspapers show the tower finished by June and standing by October. 1915 is the better-documented date for the first tower.

The November 1923 report says steel tower materials were stored for spring erection, so the register's 1923 may mark the purchase and firelookout.com's 1924 the raising. This is an inference; no source says so directly.

notes_for_editor: Height disagrees across sources: 85 ft (Nov 1923 plan), 90 ft (register and firelookout.com for the steel tower), about 100 ft (1947 survey description), and 84/90/100 ft for the timber L-4 tower. The record's height_m 25.9 (85 ft) matches only the 1923 plan; left unchanged, no height in facts. The record's design 'Aermotor' comes from the Forest Lookouts 1924 entry, not the register. Harrison spelled Wilbur in most items and Wilbert in two. No source describes remains on the summit; the Forest Service pages describe only the picnic area and trail. A local check would show whether any footings remain.
